endorsements.quote: Therefore, it is advisable to obtain solid prospective validation from external sources at different centers with adequate sample sizes, all while adhering to the transparency and ethical guidelines to overcome potential distrust concerning ML among clinicians and patients.
Adherence to this statement will improve the interpretability, reproducibility, risk of bias assessment, and ultimately its applicability in clinical practice [ 45 ].
Although it is advisable to use multiple metrics to measure performance more broadly, most studies published thus far on the use of AI for predicting complications did not adhere to this principle.
Therefore, medical tools using AI should be used in an assistive manner as opposed to being ultimately responsible for the main decision-making [ 54 ].

A prospective simulation study in which the predictive performance of a model is tested in addition to the regular local care without affecting its course would enable the correct calibration of the ML model.
When risk scores are created, it is essential that several experts in the field of surgery, nursery, or data science discuss the favorable cut-off values together.

However, to maximize the model interpretability, one could use either individual conditional expectations (ICEs), local interpretable model-agnostic explanations (LIMEs), or Shapley additive explanations (SHAPs) [ 31 ].

unlisted_practices: Train and validate ML models in multiple healthcare facilities with adequate sample sizes to ensure generalizability.
Use a uniform classification system or international consensus for postoperative complications to ensure clinical applicability and generalizability.
Estimate overfitting using repeated cross-validation or preferably bootstrap resampling with 200 to 1000 replications to obtain overoptimism-corrected performance estimates.
Ensure input data quality is accurate, available, complete, and valid.
Combine structured and unstructured data, and pre- and intraoperative data, when building postoperative complication prediction models.
Provide patient education that AI systems complement rather than replace professional decision-making.
Adhere to published governance models for ML in healthcare to ensure acceptance and ethical and legal appropriateness.
Consider implications for patients, such as over- and under-treatment, before implementing prediction models in clinical practice.
